full_text_en:
**Chu Shijian et al. — Embezzlement, Holding Huge Amounts of Property from Unidentified Sources**

**Editor's Note:** The case of Chu Shijian, former Chairman and President of Yunnan Yuxi Hongta Tobacco (Group) Co., Ltd., and others, concerning embezzlement and holding huge amounts of property from unidentified sources, has drawn to a satisfactory conclusion with the public pronouncement of Criminal Judgment (1998) Yun Gao Xing Chu Zi No. 1 of the Yunnan High People's Court, and has won widespread acclaim from all sectors of society. The successful trial of this case reflects the Party's and the state's determination to combat corruption and promote integrity, i.e., that no one, regardless of their past high position or great contributions, will escape corresponding sanctions once they violate the criminal law. At the same time, it also demonstrates the good image of China's judicial organs in adhering to the legal principles of "taking facts as the basis and law as the criterion" and enforcing the law impartially and strictly.

Judicial impartiality is the life and soul of the People's Courts' work. Whether the trial activities of the People's Courts can achieve judicial impartiality is ultimately reflected in the handling of cases, and the handling of cases is reflected through judicial documents. Therefore, judicial documents are the ultimate carrier of "judicial impartiality" and the comprehensive reproduction of the entire trial activity. This judgment of the Yunnan High Court, from content to form, departs from the previous "facts found," "opinion," and "judgment" model of many judgments, which gave people the impression that court judgments were "insufficiently reasoned" or even "unreasonable." It has become a model of fully reasoning by using facts and law under the premise of adhering to procedural justice. The judgment first separately addresses the three charges brought by the indictment against Chu Shijian and others, stating the main views and evidence of both the prosecution and the defense, objectively reproducing the focus of the dispute and the situation of evidence presentation and cross-examination. It then analyzes and evaluates the evidence through "Opinion of the Court," making findings or rejecting findings on the alleged facts, explaining the reasons and basis for such findings or rejections. Then, the court "In summary," makes a comprehensive judgment on the conviction and sentencing of Chu Shijian and others based on the accurate application of law and the specific circumstances of the case. The entire judgment has rigorous arguments, strong logic, clear hierarchy, coherence, thorough analysis, and the integration of reason, emotion, and law; the reasons and results of the judgment are clear and explicit. This not only reflects the high trial art and writing ability of the judges who tried the case but also provides a reference example for the drafting of judicial documents by People's Courts at all levels.

This year is the "Trial Quality Year" launched by courts nationwide. Improving trial quality also includes improving the quality of legal documents. We hereby publish the full text of Criminal Judgment (1998) Yun Gao Xing Chu Zi No. 1 of the Yunnan High People's Court for the reference of People's Courts at all levels, in order to further promote the deepening of trial method reform, especially the comprehensive improvement of the drafting level of legal documents. Let us work together from top to bottom, live up to the heavy trust of the Party and the people, handle more and better cases, and make greater contributions to ensuring judicial impartiality and maintaining judicial authority.

**Yunnan High People's Court**

**Criminal Judgment**

(1998) Yun Gao Xing Chu Zi No. 1

**Prosecutorial Authority:** Yunnan Provincial People's Procuratorate.

**Defendant:** Chu Shijian, male, born on February 1, 1928, Han nationality, senior high school education, native of Huaning County, Yunnan Province, former Chairman and President of Yunnan Yuxi Hongta Tobacco (Group) Co., Ltd., residing in the staff dormitory of Yuxi Cigarette Factory. Placed under residential surveillance in connection with this case on February 8, 1997, and arrested on July 10 of the same year. Currently detained in the detention center of the Yunnan Provincial Public Security Department.

**Defense Counsel:** Ma Jun and Luo Tao, lawyers of Yunnan Zhenxu Law Firm.

**Defendant:** Luo Yijun, male, born on June 13, 1953, Han nationality, college education, native of Tonghai County, Yunnan Province, former Chief Accountant of Yunnan Yuxi Hongta Tobacco (Group) Co., Ltd., residing in the staff dormitory of Yuxi Cigarette Factory. Criminally detained on August 8, 1997, in connection with this case, and arrested on August 22 of the same year. Currently detained in the detention center of the Yunnan Provincial Public Security Department.

**Defense Counsel:** Wang Beichuan and He Jing, lawyers of Yunnan Beichuan Law Firm.

**Defendant:** Qiao Fake, male, born on September 5, 1938, Han nationality, master's degree education, native of Jinning County, Yunnan Province, former Vice Chairman and Vice President of Yunnan Yuxi Hongta Tobacco (Group) Co., Ltd., residing in the staff dormitory of Yuxi Cigarette Factory. Criminally detained on August 8, 1997, in connection with this case, and arrested on August 22 of the same year. Currently detained in the detention center of the Yunnan Provincial Public Security Department.

**Defense Counsel:** Huan Rui, lawyer of Yunnan Donglu Law Firm.

On August 6, 1998, the Yunnan Provincial People's Procuratorate initiated a public prosecution with this court against the defendant Chu Shijian for the crimes of embezzlement and holding huge amounts of property from unidentified sources, and against the defendants Luo Yijun and Qiao Fake for the crime of embezzlement. Upon receipt, this court formed a collegial panel according to law and held a public hearing of this case. Procurators Zhu Jianwei, Mao Jianyi, and Zheng Bo of the Yunnan Provincial People's Procuratorate appeared in court to support the prosecution; the defendant Chu Shijian and his defense counsels Ma Jun and Luo Tao, the defendant Luo Yijun and his defense counsels Wang Beichuan and He Jing, the defendant Qiao Fake and his defense counsel Huan Rui, and witness Liu Ruilin appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. After deliberation by the collegial panel and discussion and decision by the Adjudication Committee of this court, the trial has now been concluded.

The indictment filed three charges against the defendants Chu Shijian, Luo Yijun, and Qiao Fake respectively. During the trial, the prosecution and the defense, addressing the alleged facts, charges, and related circumstances, presented evidence, conducted cross-examination, and debated in court. The three defendants made their final statements. Synthesizing the disputes of both parties and their respective reasons, this court makes the following evaluation:

**I. The indictment alleges:** From 1993 to 1994, Yuxi Cigarette Factory deposited revenues from cigarette sales (also known as floating price funds) and retained earnings from cigarette processing profits in Singapore, totaling USD 28,570,748.5, with its subsidiary, Hong Kong Huayu Trade Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Huayu Company"). Chu Shijian instructed Luo Yijun to intercept and keep these funds off the books of Yuxi Cigarette Factory and Huayu Company, and stipulated that they could only be used upon his authorized signature. In June 1995, Chu Shijian, together with Luo Yijun and Qiao Fake, planned on two occasions to first take out USD 3 million from these funds for private distribution. Chu decided that he would take over USD 1 million, Luo Yijun and Qiao Fake would each take USD 600,000 to 700,000, and Sheng Dayong (at large), General Manager of Huayu Company, and Liu Ruilin (separately prosecuted), Deputy General Manager of Huayu Company, would also receive a share, and the money would be kept in the account of Singaporean businessman Zhong Zhaoxin. On July 15, 1995, Luo Yijun, carrying four powers of attorney signed by Chu Shijian, arrived in Shenzhen, conveyed Chu's instructions to Sheng Dayong and Liu Ruilin, who agreed. Luo Yijun filled in the transfer amounts on the powers of attorney: USD 1,740,000 for Chu Shijian, USD 681,061 for Luo Yijun, USD 680,000 for Qiao Fake, and USD 450,000 for Sheng Dayong and Liu Ruilin. Luo handed the completed powers of attorney and the receiving bank account number requested from Zhong Zhaoxin to Sheng Dayong, instructing him to handle it immediately. On July 19, Sheng Dayong transferred USD 3,551,061 to Zhong Zhaoxin's account. After returning to Yuxi Cigarette Factory, Luo Yijun reported the handling to Chu Shijian and Qiao Fake. The above funds have been recovered after the case was uncovered.

Regarding this alleged fact, the prosecutorial authority read out and presented the following evidence in court:

1. Account pages of Huayu Company, to prove that Yuxi Cigarette Factory deposited USD 28,570,748.5 in sales revenue (floating price funds) and retained cigarette processing profits with Huayu Company, and the USD 3,551,061 remitted by Chu Shijian and others was part of the above funds.
2. Statements of defendants Chu Shijian, Luo Yijun, and Qiao Fake during the investigation, to prove the process of the three defendants' premeditated private distribution of US dollars.
3. Adjustment vouchers of Huayu Company, adjustment remarks recorded by Liu Ruilin, Deputy General Manager of Huayu Company, and Liu Ruilin's testimony, to prove the process of defendant Luo Yijun holding the power of attorney signed by defendant Chu Shijian to make adjustments at Huayu Company.
4. Bank transfer vouchers and bank receipt vouchers, to prove the time and amount of remittance from Huayu Company, as well as the receiving bank and account number.
5. Testimony of Singaporean businessman Zhong Zhaoxin, to prove the process of defendant Chu Shijian and others depositing the funds into his account at HSBC in Hong Kong.
6. Seizure vouchers, to prove that all funds were recovered after the case was uncovered.

The prosecutorial authority submits that the defendants Chu Shijian, Luo Yijun, and Qiao Fake, by taking advantage of their positions, jointly embezzled public funds in an especially huge amount, thus all constituting the crime of embezzlement. In the joint crime, defendant Chu Shijian initiated the criminal intent, played a directing role, and is the principal offender; defendant Luo Yijun carried out the transfer of funds, and defendant Qiao Fake participated in the private distribution, both being accessories.

The facts stated in court by defendants Chu Shijian, Luo Yijun, and Qiao Fake are substantially consistent with the alleged facts. Defendant Chu Shijian submitted that the amount premeditated for private distribution differs from the amount alleged for embezzlement. The defense counsel for defendant Chu Shijian raised three objections to the indictment: First, there is a contradiction between the amounts reflected by various pieces of evidence and the amount determined in the indictment; the indictment determined the amount of US dollars each of the three defendants individually embezzled, which is supported only by Luo Yijun's confession, with no other evidence to corroborate. Second, the funds privately distributed by the three defendants were floating price funds from cigarette sales, which were off-book funds, and the decision to distribute was made collectively, so it should be characterized as the crime of collectively distributing state-owned assets; the charge of embezzlement cannot be sustained. Third, the funds were transferred to the account of Singaporean businessman Zhong Zhaoxin, and the defendants did not actually take possession, so it constitutes an attempted crime.

The defense counsel for defendant Luo Yijun submitted that defendant Chu Shijian instructed defendant Luo Yijun to transfer USD 3,551,061 from Huayu Company's account to the bank account of Singaporean businessman Zhong Zhaoxin in Hong Kong; this act merely created conditions for the three defendants' private distribution, the funds were not controlled by each person according to the premeditated shares, the nature of the public funds did not change, and afterwards all funds were returned in the name of Yuxi Cigarette Factory; therefore, the acts of the three defendants constitute preparation for a crime. The defense counsel for defendant Qiao Fake submitted that defendant Qiao Fake only expressed criminal intent, did not commit any criminal act, and did not actually take possession of the privately distributed US dollars; therefore, the charge of embezzlement against him cannot be sustained.

**Opinion of the Court:** The basic facts that the defendants Chu Shijian, Luo Yijun, and Qiao Fake jointly embezzled public funds of USD 3,551,061 are clear, and the basic evidence is sufficient, and the three defendants have also confessed. Regarding the disputed amount, this court confirms the fact that when the three defendants planned to privately distribute US dollars, they agreed on over USD 1 million for Chu Shijian, and USD 600,000 to 700,000 each for Luo Yijun and Qiao Fake, and ultimately actually transferred USD 3,551,061.

Regarding the view of the defense counsel for defendant Chu Shijian that the crime should be characterized as collectively distributing state-owned assets, this court holds that the crime of collectively distributing state-owned assets is a unit crime, the subject of the crime is the unit, and the objective aspect of the crime is characterized by a decision of the unit and collective distribution. The defendants Chu Shijian, Luo Yijun, and Qiao Fake, with the purpose of illegal personal possession, taking advantage of their positions, and using secret methods to embezzle public funds, is neither an act of the unit nor a collective distribution, and does not conform to the basic characteristics of the crime of collectively distributing state-owned assets. Therefore, this opinion of the defense counsel is not adopted.

Regarding the view of the defense counsel for defendant Chu Shijian that it constitutes an attempted crime, the view of the defense counsel for defendant Luo Yijun that it constitutes preparation for a crime, and the view of the defense counsel for defendant Qiao Fake that Qiao Fake's act constitutes an expression of criminal intent, this court holds that the three defendants subjectively had the intent to jointly embezzle public funds, and objectively had already transferred the public funds from Huayu Company's bank account to Zhong Zhaoxin's account. After this process was completed, Yuxi Cigarette Factory and Huayu Company both lost possession and control over the funds, the actual right of control was with the defendants, and the ownership of the funds was illegally infringed upon. The acts of the three defendants meet all the constitutive elements of the crime of embezzlement and constitute a completed crime. Therefore, the opinions of the three defense counsels are not adopted.

In summary, the defendants Chu Shijian, Luo Yijun, and Qiao Fake, by taking advantage of their positions, jointly embezzled public funds of USD 3,551,061 (equivalent to RMB 28,741,577 according to the foreign exchange rate of the day), and their acts have constituted the crime of embezzlement, with an especially huge amount. In the joint crime, defendant Chu Shijian played a principal role and is the principal offender; defendants Luo Yijun and Qiao Fake are accessories. The basic facts and charges alleged by the prosecutorial authority are established, and this court confirms them.

**II. The indictment alleges:** In mid-November 1995, Chu Shijian instructed Luo Yijun to destroy the bank account and related materials of the off-book floating price funds held by Huayu Company, and to transfer the remaining over USD 11.5 million in full under the name of "payment for equipment parts." Chu decided that he would take over USD 11.5 million, and gave Luo Yijun a bank receiving account number typed in English provided by Zhong Zhaoxin, instructing him to transfer the money to that account. Luo Yijun noted USD 11.56 million on the account number given by Chu Shijian, and together with the power of attorney signed by Chu Shijian, went to Shenzhen to find Sheng Dayong, General Manager of Huayu Company, instructing him to handle it immediately. On January 23, 1996, the account provided by Zhong Zhaoxin to Chu Shijian received USD 11.56 million. The above funds have been fully recovered after the case was uncovered.

Regarding this alleged fact, the prosecutorial authority read out and presented in court: bank transfer vouchers, bank receipt vouchers, testimony of witnesses Luo Yijun, Liu Ruilin, and Zhong Zhaoxin, to prove the process of defendant Chu Shijian instructing Luo Yijun to transfer USD 11.56 million from Huayu Company's bank account to the account opened by Singaporean businessman Zhong Zhaoxin in an overseas bank. Defendant Chu Shijian and his defense counsel have no objection to the fact of the transfer.

Defendant Chu Shijian argued: The reason for instructing Luo Yijun to destroy the bank account holding the floating price funds and transfer the remaining balance of over USD 15 million in full to Zhong Zhaoxin's account was that he was about to hand over his work and wanted to cover up the fact of the private distribution of USD 3.55 million; the funds were transferred out for Yuxi Cigarette Factory to pay for the purchase of tobacco expansion equipment, not for himself.

The defense counsel submits that the evidence is insufficient to prove defendant Chu Shijian's subjective intent of illegal possession.

In response to defendant Chu Shijian's argument and the defense counsel's opinion, the prosecutorial authority further read out and presented the following evidence:

1. Testimony of Luo Yijun, proving that "Chu Shijian said he wanted USD 11.5 million for himself"; and also proving that "Chu Shijian gave me a bank account number typed in English for transferring funds."
2. Testimony of Zhong Zhaoxin, proving that "Chu told me he wanted to transfer a sum of money to my account and asked me for an account number... I specifically bought a company, opened a bank account, and provided the account to Chu; the funds were transferred to this account."
3. Contracts and payment vouchers, proving that the payment for the tobacco expansion equipment that defendant Chu Shijian argued was paid through other channels.

The prosecutorial authority submits that the above evidence fully confirms defendant Chu Shijian's subjective intent of illegal possession, and his argument cannot stand. Therefore, defendant Chu Shijian's act has constituted the crime of embezzlement.

Defendant Chu Shijian expressed objections to the testimony of Luo Yijun and Zhong Zhaoxin. The defense counsel submits that there are significant contradictions in the testimony of Luo Yijun and Zhong Zhaoxin, and they cannot serve as the basis for finding the facts.

The court summoned Luo Yijun to testify in court according to law. During his testimony in court, Luo Yijun testified that Chu Shijian said the transferred US dollars were intended as sponsorship funds and for other expenses.

**Opinion of the Court:** The fact that defendant Chu Shijian instructed Luo Yijun to transfer USD 11.56 million from Huayu Company's account to Zhong Zhaoxin's overseas bank account is clear and undisputed by both parties. The focus of the dispute is whether the evidence is sufficient to prove defendant Chu Shijian's subjective intent of illegal possession; the essence of the dispute is whether defendant Chu Shijian's act meets the subjective element of the crime of embezzlement and constitutes the crime of embezzlement. Upon examination:

1. The testimony of Luo Yijun cannot serve as the basis for finding the facts. Luo Yijun directly carried out the fund transfer and had a stake in this charge. When testifying as a witness, his testimony was inconsistent, particularly, the content of his testimony in court significantly differed from his testimony given before trial, with self-contradictions on key points. He could not provide a reasonable explanation for the challenges raised by the defense counsel, and his testimony was not corroborated by other evidence. Therefore, Luo Yijun's testimony is not admitted.
2. The testimony of Zhong Zhaoxin also cannot serve as the basis for finding the facts. The part of his testimony concerning specifically buying a company and opening a bank account for defendant Chu Shijian to transfer funds, upon verification, contained contradictions in timing and purpose; regarding providing the account number to defendant Chu Shijian, there were multiple versions, which were inconsistent and not corroborated by other evidence. Therefore, Zhong Zhaoxin's testimony is not admitted.
3. The evidence such as contracts and payment vouchers presented by the prosecutorial authority can only prove that the payment for the tobacco expansion equipment was not made from the transferred USD 11.56 million, but cannot directly prove defendant Chu Shijian's intent of illegal possession. Since the testimony of Luo Yijun and Zhong Zhaoxin is not admitted, the evidence of the charge cannot corroborate each other to form a chain of evidence.

According to the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law, in criminal proceedings, the prosecution bears the burden of providing evidence to prove the crime. If the evidence is insufficient, the charge cannot be established. In this charge, the evidence reflects that defendant Chu Shijian had a subjective intent when transferring the funds, but the possibility of illegal possession, purchase of equipment, or other purposes simultaneously exists, lacking sufficient exclusivity. Therefore, the evidence for charging defendant Chu Shijian with embezzling USD 11.56 million is insufficient, and this court does not confirm it.

**III. The indictment alleges:** From August 1995 to July 1998, during the investigation of this case, the Luoyang Public Security Bureau and the Yunnan Provincial People's Procuratorate seized and froze property of Chu Shijian, including currency, gold products, houses, and other valuables, in Kunming City and Yuxi City of Yunnan Province, and Yanshi City of Henan Province, totaling an equivalent of RMB 5.21 million and HKD 620,000. Of this, Chu Shijian can explain the legitimate sources of income that have been verified as RMB 1.18 million. For the remaining property totaling RMB 4.03 million and HKD 620,000, Chu Shijian cannot explain their legitimate sources. Upon investigation, no legitimate sources have been found.

Regarding this alleged fact, the prosecutorial authority presented and read out in court: 18 seized deposit slips, 82 pieces of gold products, 2 "Rolex" gold watches, HKD 230,000, RMB 9,200, photos of 4 commercial apartments, purchase agreements, payment vouchers, and property value appraisal certificates, testimony of witnesses Ma Jingfang, Ma Jingheng, Ma Jingfen, Li Xiangyun, Yu Bin, et al., as well as relevant proof of defendant Chu Shijian's legitimate income.

The prosecutorial authority submits that defendant Chu Shijian, for the portion of his huge property that clearly exceeds his legitimate income, cannot explain its legitimate sources, and upon investigation, no legitimate sources are found; his act has constituted the crime of holding huge amounts of property from unidentified sources.

Defendant Chu Shijian has no objection to the evidence of the charge but submits that part of the above property was gifted by foreign businessmen.

The defense counsel submits that the legitimate property of defendant Chu Shijian's wife from the joint property of the couple should be deducted.

In response to the objections of defendant Chu Shijian and the defense counsel, the prosecutorial authority further explains that defendant Chu Shijian failed to accurately state the facts regarding the alleged gifts from foreign businessmen, and also failed to provide clues such as the names and addresses of the foreign businessmen for verification; it cannot be verified, and his argument cannot stand. As for the legitimate property of defendant Chu Shijian's wife from the joint property of the couple, the indictment has already made deductions when determining it.

**Opinion of the Court**

Pursuant to the law, the defendant Chu Shijian bears the burden of proof with respect to the portion of his property that obviously exceeds lawful income. The explanations and defenses of the defendant Chu Shijian are not supported by verifiable facts, and his defenses cannot be established. The charges brought by the prosecutorial authority are based on clear facts and sufficient evidence, and the crimes are established. This Court hereby affirms them.

Furthermore, the prosecutorial authority also determined that the defendant Chu Shijian had voluntarily surrendered and performed major meritorious service, and that the defendant Luo Yijun had performed meritorious service and major meritorious service, and presented relevant evidence in court.

The defendants Chu Shijian, Luo Yijun, and Qiao Fake, and their defense counsel, raised no objections to the above determinations.

The defense counsel for the defendant Chu Shijian argued that Chu Shijian had made significant contributions to the development of the Yuxi Cigarette Factory and to the provincial economy, and that his meritorious service should be fully considered at sentencing, with lenient treatment.

The defense counsel for the defendant Qiao Fake argued that Qiao Fake had voluntarily surrendered, and had previously made relatively significant contributions to the development of the Yuxi Cigarette Factory, and that leniency should be considered.

In response to the arguments raised by the defense counsel, the prosecutorial authority submitted that the defendants Chu Shijian and Qiao Fake had indeed made important contributions to the Yuxi Cigarette Factory, but that meritorious service cannot offset criminal punishment, and all are equal before the law in its application. The defendant Qiao Fake confessed to the crime only after the investigative authorities had already discovered the criminal facts and interrogated him, which does not constitute voluntary surrender.

This Court, upon review, holds: The defendant Chu Shijian, during the period when he was subjected to compulsory measures for suspected other crimes, before the judicial authorities had fully discovered the facts of the joint embezzlement of USD 3,551,061 by the defendants Chu Shijian, Luo Yijun, and Qiao Fake, confessed to this criminal fact, which shall be deemed voluntary surrender; during the investigation period, he reported major criminal leads concerning others, which were verified to be true, constituting major meritorious service. The defendant Luo Yijun, during the investigation period, reported leads concerning others' embezzlement of public property, but the reported facts were not subject to criminal prosecution, and meritorious service cannot be established; with respect to major meritorious service, it refers to the defendant Luo Yijun reporting the major criminal fact of the defendant Chu Shijian embezzling USD 11.56 million. Since this Court does not affirm this charge against Chu Shijian, the defendant Luo Yijun's major meritorious service cannot be established either. However, this act enabled the prosecutorial authorities to promptly recover huge amounts of state assets lost abroad, which may be considered as a discretionary mitigating circumstance at sentencing. The defendant Qiao Fake, after a co-defendant had already confessed the joint criminal facts to the prosecutorial authorities, made a truthful confession when interrogated by the investigators; this does not constitute a voluntary surrender and voluntary surrender cannot be established, but may be considered as a circumstance of having a good attitude in admitting guilt, with discretionary leniency.

Regarding the defense opinion raised by counsel that the defendants Chu Shijian and Qiao Fake had made significant contributions to the Yuxi Cigarette Factory and should be given a lighter punishment, this Court holds: During their tenure as leaders of the Yuxi Cigarette Factory, the defendants Chu Shijian and Qiao Fake made contributions to the development of the "Yuyan" brand, for which the Party and the government granted them political and material honors and treatment. However, no matter how great the contribution, it does not entitle them to privileges beyond the law. All are equal before the law, and any citizen who commits a crime shall be subject to criminal prosecution in accordance with the law. Article 61 of the Criminal Law of the PRC provides that when deciding the penalty for a criminal offender, the sentence shall be imposed based on the facts, nature, and circumstances of the crime, and the degree of harm to society, in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Law. The defendants Chu Shijian and Qiao Fake used their official positions to embezzle public funds in an extremely large amount, which constitutes exceptionally serious circumstances. This is the basis for the criminal liability of the defendants, and the penalty must be commensurate with the crime committed. As for the subjective circumstances reflected in the defendants' historical performance, these may be considered as appropriate at sentencing.

In conclusion, this Court holds: The defendants Chu Shijian, Luo Yijun, and Qiao Fake, by taking advantage of their official positions, privately divided public funds amounting to USD 3,551,061, equivalent to RMB 28.7 million. Their actions have all constituted the crime of embezzlement, and the amounts involved are extremely large, with exceptionally serious circumstances. The defendant Chu Shijian played a decisive and organizational role in the joint crime and is the principal offender, who shall be held responsible for all crimes he organized and participated in, and should be sentenced to death in accordance with the law. However, in light of his voluntary surrender and major meritorious service, and the fact that all illicit funds have been recovered, the economic losses have been remedied, and other circumstances, the punishment shall be mitigated in accordance with the law. The defendant Chu Shijian also committed the crime of possessing a huge amount of property from unexplained sources, and shall be subject to combined punishment for several offenses in accordance with the law. The defendant Luo Yijun actively participated in the crime, specifically implemented the fund transfer actions, and played a significant role. However, in light of the fact that he was an accessory, confessed the criminal facts after the incident came to light, reported the illegal acts of others, and had a good attitude in admitting guilt, the punishment may be mitigated in accordance with the law. The defendant Qiao Fake, who was invited to participate in the crime, was an accessory, played a relatively minor role in the joint criminal activity, confessed the criminal facts after the incident came to light, and had a good attitude in admitting guilt, the punishment may be mitigated in accordance with the law. Accordingly, this Court, in order to protect public property from infringement, maintain the socialist economic order, and severely punish serious economic crimes, based on the facts, nature, circumstances, and degree of harm to society of each defendant's crime, in accordance with Articles 12, 382(1), 383(1)(1), 26(1)&(4), 27, 57(1), 67, 68, 69 of the Criminal Law of the PRC, and Article 11(1) of the Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Punishing the Crimes of Embezzlement and Bribery, hereby renders the following judgment:

1. The defendant Chu Shijian is sentenced to life imprisonment for the crime of embezzlement, with deprivation of political rights for life, and confiscation of property in the amount of RMB 200,000; for the crime of possessing a huge amount of property from unexplained sources, he is sentenced to five years of imprisonment; for the combined punishment for several offenses, the sentence is life imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for life, and confiscation of property in the amount of RMB 200,000.

2. The portion of the defendant Chu Shijian's huge property that obviously exceeds lawful income, valued at RMB 4,030,000 and HKD 620,000, is to be confiscated in accordance with the law.

3. The defendant Luo Yijun is sentenced to 14 years of imprisonment for the crime of embezzlement, with confiscation of property in the amount of RMB 130,000.

4. The defendant Qiao Fake is sentenced to 5 years of imprisonment for the crime of embezzlement, with confiscation of property in the amount of RMB 50,000.

If any party is not satisfied with this judgment, they may, within ten days from the day following receipt of the written judgment, file an appeal with this Court or directly with the Supreme People's Court of the People's Republic of China.
